newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission set to adopt cohesion report on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Commission set to adopt cohesion report on Wednesday.

text.p: The European Commission is set to adopt on Wednesday an in-depth progress report on cohesion in the European Union, EU sources said on Monday.
It will show that progress has been made in reducing gaps in living standards but also that some policy changes will be needed, one source said.
"(The report) will say that we are on the right track."

The report -- which covers the 10 years up to 1993 -- looks at trends in cohesion between member states, regions and social groups and at how and whether member states' policies and EU policies have contributed to boost regional development.

The report will provide a basis for a future look at how the structural funds will be affected by the enlargement towards poorer eastern and central European countries. But it does not explicitly elaborate on the impact of enlargement.
Under article 130b of the Maastricht treaty the Commission must submit every three years a report on the progress "made towards achieving economic and social cohesion".
If necessary, it says the report should be accompanied by "appropriate proposals".
It will be the first time such a report has been made and concrete work on enlargement and regional policy would start only after the report is published.
The structural funds are the EU's primary vehicle for promoting economic and social balance and reducing regional disparities among the 15 member states.
For the 1994-1999 period the funds' allocation amounts to 141 billion Ecus.
